entries.content:
Over the years I have helped Dionne Warwick to find physicians for
herself and her colleagues.   I have done this sometimes through as intermediary, Guy 
Draper, who is well-known sould song wsriter and agent for many groups.   Guy 
called me up today and asked for a referral for a peripheral vascular physician at Hopkins 
for one of Dionne’s friends.   I recommended in Medicine Dr. Elizabeth Virginia 
Ratchford and in Surgery Dr. James Hamilton Black.   Also, Guy wanted me to put on 
my calendar for June 13, 2020 a ceremony at Bowie State University where they are 
dedicating a building to Dionne.   They want me there as their guest.
Also, Jon laPook was interviewed on CBS Morning News and mentioned me several 
times since he e-mail me over the weekend to prep him for his interview on Universal Flu 
vaccine and HIV vaccines.

Met in my office with Dr. Olivier Tshiani who was and is a main player
in our PALM trial in DRC.   Also present were Cliff lane, Rick Davey and Lori Dodd.  
Olivier was right there on site when the Mai Mai burned the ETUs at Katwa and 
Butembo and his car was stoned as he was travelling at night from the ETU to his 
compound where he was living in Butembo.   He related stories of the very difficult 
security issues while doing the PALM study.   He is a real hero.   He had also previously 
spent 5 years in Nancy Sullivan’s lab. Here at VRC.
Did TV interview with Cox TV this year’s influenza situation.   Interviewed by 
Samantha Manning

Influenza is heavy in the media.   Did an interview with Elizabeth Cohen
of CNN for her Blog.   Also, did a live radio interview with John Catsimatidis for his 
“Cats Roundtable” from NYC.
Also, yesterday the US via a precise drone strike in Iraq outside of Baghdad airport 
killed the leader of the Iranian Quds Force General Quassim Souleimani.   There has 
been over the past few days attacks on the US Embassy by Iranian backed Iraqi militia as 
a result of the fact that the US armed forces attacked and killed 25 Iranian backed Iraqi 
militia who had killed a USA contractor and wounded several USA soldiers in Iraq.  This 
will certainly lead to major escalation of tension and even retaliation from Iran.
Also 44 unusual cases of pneumonia in Wuhan, China opver the past couple of days.   
Etiology still unknown.   Said to be a “viral pneumonia’ of unknown etiology.   Flu ruled 
out.   Cases linked to a seafood market.  No human-to-human transmission documented at 
this time.

Chris and I went to a book party for our friend Ruth Marcus
(Washington Post columnist), fo her book “Supreme Ambition” about Justice Brett 
Kavanaugh.   Party at the home of David and Katherine Bradley at 2211 30th Street, NW.   
Elegant home.   Super A list at party: Senator Mark Warner, Kellyanne Conway, Andrea 
Mitchell, David Ignatius, David Frum, Zeke Emanuel, etc., etc.  Rafe Sagalyn is Ruth’s 
agent and was there.   Also, ran into Sylvia Burwell.   Really great to see her. Realized 
how much I miss working with her.  Nice evening.

Just because of the sudden preduction of 1-3 inches of snow, OPM shut
down the USG at 1:00 PM and everyone rushed to get off campus at the same time that 
Walter Reed personnel are trying to leave.   This has created a total nightmare traffic jam 
on campus.   It is taking almost 1 hour to get off campus from time you get in your car.
Did TV interview with Canadian TV (CTV) on the viral outbreak in Wuhan, China.  
Did interview (print) with HealthDay on the influenza season

(Friday)– Infleunza is hot and heavy.   Vaccine match is OK for H1N1,
but not so good for B and H3N2.   Did WUSA local TV on flu as well as interview with 
Elizabeth Cohen of CNN that went on her blog with multiple references to our 
conversation.
Appeared on Voice of America to discuss the new Wuhan virus documented to be a 
novel coronavirus.  Interesting that ovewr the past several years we have had 3 emerging 
novel coronaviruses that have caused serious disease in humans: SARS, MERS, and now 
the Wuhan virus.
 
Chinese publish sequence of the virus on public data base

(Saturday) – Barney Graham ordersd the constructs using credit
cards.

Went to a function at the National Cathedral where David Rubenstein
was interview in the naïve (similar to my interview a few years ago) by the Dean of the 
Cathedral in association with David’s book – “The American Story”.  David was his 
usual hilarious self.

Barney Graham’s team starts work on GMP vaccine in
collaboration with Moderna
 Did taped interview for the Islam Radio Breakfast Show about anti-vaxx movement.   
Very good interview.
Also, did another interview with Eileen Reilly of Axios
Apparently, CDC is upset because I am saying that this is on a course to be as bad a year 
as 2017-2018 and 2014-2015.  In fact, the flu infection “numbers” are exactly on tract 
with those years.   However, there are less total deaths and hospitalizations.   This is due 
to the fact that Influenza B has predominated early that this hits kids more severely.  
Since the elderly account for most of the deaths and hospitalizations, the total of these are 
down; however for this time compared to other years, the number of pediatric deaths is 
way up.   And so it depends what you mean by a ‘bad’ season.  I say it is a bad season 
and CDC says no. There was a discussion between Azar and Nancy Messonnier of CDC 
about this and about my statements, but no one thought of getting me on the conference 
call.   Not good.   Typical CDC!

Did interview on WTOP Radio on the number of pediatric flu deaths.
I explained the issue of predominance of Influenza B and children and the poor match of 
the vaccine to circulating virus with Influenza B Victoria.

The situation in Wuhan, China continues.   Now have 2 deaths and 2
cases in Thailand and 1 in Japan.   Was in on a PCC meeting via the NIH SCIF with the 
NSC chaired by Anthony Ruggiero.  CDC and DHS have decided to do entry screening at 
3 USA airport in people coming directly and indirectly from Wuhan: Kennedy in NYC, 
LAX, and SFO.   Tomorrow night at 10:00 PM a 747 from Wuhan will arrive at Kennedy 
and will be the first to get screened.

AL.docx
I appeared this evening on a PBS NewsHour segment on Ebola with considerable 
exposure in the piece.

appeared on radio with NPR “Here and Now” on the pediatric
Influenza B situation.   Influenza B predominating yet the Victoria B in the vaccine is 
only a 58% match and so children are getting a double whammy with B 
predominating early in the year and continuing and the vaccine is not well matched.   In 
this regard, there are more pediatric deaths (39) thus far at this point in the season 
compared to most other years.   The infection slope is high for all infections yet the total 
deaths and hospitalization are not that high, likely because there is little H3N2 and that is 
the virus that affects the elderly the most and the elderly accound for most of the 
hospitalizations and deaths.
Jennifer Ashton of ABC World News Tonight called me in a panic about 15 minutes 
before she is to go on the air about the Wuhan virus (2019nCoV).   She wanted to get my 
take on the airport screening and the potential seriousness of the situation.   I emphasized 
that we need to take this seriously and the airport screening is entirely appropriate.
We are now doing entry screening at JFK, LAX and SFO of flights from Wuhan.   There 
are a couple of direct flights per week from Wuhan to JFK and SFO

Situation starting toheaten up re: 2019nCoV.  There are now 17 more
cases in Wuhan and the LSTMH has estimated that there may actually be several 
hundreds of cases that have not yet been recognized.   It is starting to look like there is 
some low grade close contact transmission person to person.   I appeared on CNN 
Newsroom with Fredricka Whitfield to discuss the 2019 nCoV situation and the recent 
screening at 3 airports.

Things evolving rapidly with the 2019 nCoV.   Now there are 198
confirmed cases, all in China except for 2 in Thailand and 1 in Japan.  Cases now in 
Guangdong Province with suspected cases in Beijing and Shanghai.  
Did TV interview (pre-taped) for CNN International at 10:00 PM to be shown 
internationally through the night and tomorrow,

Now there are >220 cases of n-CoV with a travel case in South Korea
and 14 transmissions to health care providers.  Clearly, this is a rapidly expanding 
situation with no question about person-to-person transmission.
Did print interview for Caixin Media Company, which is the most influential political 
and business news organization in China.
Also did interview for CBS Evening News and for FOX 5 Local TV
Also, conversation with Elizabeth Cohen of CNN.  Problem with her is that she tends to 
dramatize things, which can get me in trouble not matter how many caveats I give her.

n-CoV situation continues to evolve.   Now 298 cases with 6 deaths.
Very fluid.
Did ointerview with Eileen O’Reilly for Axios
Interview with Chinese Radio Free Asia
CDC announced today that the first case of n-CoV has been identified in Seattle.   A 
35 year old otherwise healthy Chinese man visited Wuhan, came to USA on January 15 
(before airport screening), developed sxs on Jan. 16, tested on Jan. 19, test sent to CDC 
and positive on Jan. 20.   He walked into a clinical with fever and respiratory sxs and was 
smart enough to mention that he just came from Wuhan.
Other press today – VOA News; WSJ with Betsy MacKay; WCBS Radio; TV 
NewsMAX; TV FOX Business with Lou Dodd; Biocentury with Steve Usdin; 
Bloomberg Law with Jeannie Baumann; Washington Times; Time Magazine (Alice 
Park)
We are having daily PCCs with Anthony Ruggierro.   He is his usual prickly self.

Now 400 cases and 9 deaths.  Chicago ORD and Atl airports added to
entry screening with JFK, LAX, and SFO.   Soon to funnel all flights with people from 
Wuhan (indirect) through these 5 airports.
Another PCC with Anthony being hostile that the orgs (CDC, DHS, CBP) have not 
worked out how to get 100% of people coming from Wuhan screened.  We are in Phase 1 
(Screening at JFK, LAX, SFO).   We are almost fully ready for Phase 2 (add ORD and 
ATL).  Phase 3 is to funnel people who originate at Wuhan and want to go to USA 
through one of the 5 airports.  Phase 4 is to screen individuals coming from many cities in 
China.   Big argument between CDC (Redfield) and CBP/DHS regarding have 5 versus 
12 USA airports do the screening.   Marty Cetron was trying to explain how difficult 
doing 12 USA airports would be since CDC does not have staff in a few of these cities.
To complicate it all, while we were in the PCC, China announced that it is cutting off all 
public transportation  (air, ferries, train, buses, out of Wuhan City)  Essentially a 
quarantine of the entire city of 11 million people except for absolute emergencies.   This 
complicates the USA airport screening strategy since people will not be able to get out of 
Wuhan and to the USA easily. May try other means.   Some confusion about what the 
best way to prevent establishment of infection in the USA.   Anthony (with his attitude) is 
making matters worse.   
Phase I—Current Posture
• Description: Foreign nationals who have been in China within 14 days prior to their 
actual or attempted entry into the United States are ineligible for admission under 
Section 212 (f) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA).  Departments and 
agencies may exercise certain exemptions.  Any person, but specifically U.S. 
citizens and legal permanent residents (LPRs) who have been: (1) in Hubei 
province within the past 14 days may be subject to 14 day mandatory quarantine; 
and (2) in China (outside Hubei province) within the past 14 days may be subject 
to screening and self-isolation for 14 days.  All direct and indirect flights from 
China are funneled to 11 airports with enhanced CDC medical screening.  CDC is 
coordinating with state and local health care clinicians to identify domestic cases, 
isolate cases, and conduct appropriate contact tracing.
o Triggers: Already being implemented.
• Objectives: (1) Contain the outbreak at its source, (2) minimize domestic 
importation of additional cases, (3) limit potential for domestic epidemic, and (4) 
prepare the domestic response mechanisms.
• Messaging: Daily HHS and CDC briefings and on camera task force briefings as 
appropriate.
On the interview below (FOX Business with David Asman) one of the panel asked me to 
comment of a clip he played where Trump said that everything is under control.   Xi 
Jinping told him everything is under control.   I had to answer that we are taking this very 
seriously and that Americans should not be frightened or worry, but we are taking it 
seriously.   Let us see if this pits me against the POTUS.
552 cases – 17 Deaths   Cases now in Hong Kong and Macao
WTOP Radio on Seattle case;  The Morning Goods (local radio talk show); TRT 
World Turkish TV; Reuters TV; Fox Business (Cavuto); Bloomberg print; FOX 
Business with David Asman; Italian TV (Mediaset);  Taped CNN in the VRC 
talking about the vaccine; Hong Kong Phoenix TV; Univision TV (Spanish-
American TV); Bloomberg TV Asia; 24 NEWS Israeli TV over the phone

China shuts down public transportation in 3 additional smaller cities –
Huanggang, Ezhou and Chibi.  
After 2nd Advisory Committee meeting WHO still does not declare PHEIC.   Very 
controversial decision.   They are getting some criticism about this.   On several of the 
media that I did (see below) I was asked my opinion of this.   I said I did not want to 
outguess the WHO and demurred.
Press still heavy.   Did FOX Business TV (Varney and Company); FOX News 
(Sandra Smith); CBS Radio;Shanghai Media TV via Skype; Politico (Sarah 
Owermohle); Shanghai Media TV; Science News print; CNN Newsroom (clip shown 
by Sanjay Gupta); FOX News Rundown (Radio); COX Media TV; John 
Catsimatidis Radio Show – Cats Roundtable; CNBC Asia Squawk Box; BBC radio; 
FOX Business News (Lou Dobbs);Canadian Broadcasting System (Kelly Crowe).

More cities shut down by the Chinese.   Now >800 cases and 26 deaths.
State Department issued Level 4 (no travel at all) for Wuhan.
Had meeting at EEOB381 (Anthony’s office) to discuss the evolving siautaion with 
2019-nCoV.  Derek Kan (Deputy Director, OMB) was there with other OMB folks to 
determine what the budgetary needs would be for our response.   I will put together some 
budget numbers.  I was supposed to be on this coming weekend (it is now Friday) This 
Week With George Stephanopoulos and Face the Nation; however, these were bumped 
because of impeachment trial that is onging.   
Call from Lena Sun (Washington Post) trying to verify (I said I knew nothing of this) 
that people in the USG were saying that the Chinese got to Tedros to convince him not to 
declare a PHEIC since it would harm their reputation.   I told her that was nonsense and I 
probably stopped her from writing the story.   She said since I am in all the important 
meetings that I would know.
CNBC Squawk Box; CBS Radio New York;  Massive press interactions prior to and 
after my briefing of the Senators;  Clip of me on CBS This Morning from the 
briefing

now more than1400 cases and 42 deaths.   President Xi Jinping
essentially sutting down the entire country.   Schools closing in Beijing.   Suspicion that 
the Chinese are telling us everything that is going on in China.   Why are the Chinese 
reacting so dramatically by essentially shutting down the entire country?
State Department evacuating all USA personnel from consulate in WUHAN
New York Times interview; CNN International

GAME ON!!!   Things are changing rapidly.  Dr. Ma Xiaowei, the
Chinese Minister of Health gave a press statement saying that the incubationperiod of 
nCoV is 1 to 14 days and that the virus is being transmitted when people are 
asymptomatic!   This has enormous implications for how we handle people from Wuhan 
(like our diplomats who are now on the way back from WUHAN, having been ordered to 
evaculate).   Should we quarantine them.   I am very skeptical about the Chinese 
interprepation of their data.  I spoke with Mike Ryan (WHO) from Geneva and he and 
Tedros are going to Wuhan soon.   Mike is very skeptical that aymptomatic spread is 
present or at worst is a major driver of spread.   Mike Osterholm also feels this way.  
    I spoke with Nancy Messonnier and Bob Redfield this AM to coordinate our 
responses.   Bob and I feel (and I told Elizabeth Cohen this) that we should be allowed to 
send our CDC epidemiologists to China to work with them so that we see the data first 
hand since we will base important response activities and strategies based on whether this 
is true.   It would require our quarantining for a period of time even asymptomatic people 
who arrive from Wuhan.
It now appears using epi data and genomic data that the first infection was in early 
December and was not connected to the market.   The infections spread among people 
weeks before the Chinese reported that they were dealing with a new infection and that 
gave the virus time to establish itself in multigenerational (sustained) spread.   
Remember, early on the Chinese were saying that there is no human to human 
transmission and all the original 27 cases were from the market.   Now we know the 
market was not the source, it was the amplifier.   Having said that, somewhere the virus 
jumped from animals to humans.
There is complete chaos in China now with president Xi Jinping declaring an emergency 
situation.   The Chinese are building within days 1000 and 1300 bed hospitals and flying 
in hundreds of medical personnel from military.  They have shut down travel within most 
of the country and have called off many Lunar New Year events.   Schools closed at least 
until mid-February.   Running out of supplies such as PPE.
Had 8:00 PM call with Anthony Ruggiero, Phil Ferro, and Bob Redfield about the 
evolving situation.  The deputiers and White House are pushing to close the borders for 
any traffic from China.   Bob and I are against that.   Anthony said that he heard that I wa 
in favor of that.   Will have 11:00 AM meeting tomorrow from SCIF with Deputy 
National Security Advisor Matthew Pottinger regarding possibly closing borders from 
China entry.
CNN phone interview with Elizabeth Cohen; CBC Canadian TV; CNN with 
Fredricka Whitfield (cancelled because of tragic accidental death of Kob Bryant in 
helicopter crash in LA); NewsHour from UK

Packed day today.  Council and multiple important non-corona-virus
meetings.
Busy day – two meeting with White House via SCIF.   First at 11:00 AM led by Deputy 
Director NSC Matt Pottinger who still wants to stop all incoming from China.   Bob 
Redfield, Phil Ferro, Mart Cetron, Peter Marks etc.
Second White House meeting via SCIF was on same subject withMick Mulvaney 
Chairing and visit to meeting by VP Pence. Still discussing the pros and cons of shutting 
off China.   I tried to squeeze in my opinion, but it was touch since I was remote.   I 
briefed Azar beforehand by phone as to the down side (historically) in shutting out a 
country.  Also at the meeting were Joe Grogan, Matt Pottinger, Alex Azar, DHS
Multiple print media including Washington Post,  Maggie Fox, Los Angeles; NPR 
Morning Edition with Rachel Martin; WTOP radio; John LaPook with CBS – 
taped interview to run with face to face interview tomorrow with Norah O’Donnell; 
VOA; CNN International; Bret Baier FOX; WTOP again; Sean Hannity (FOX);

Big day at White House.   Major discussions at Deputies on how to
handle the 200 US Citizens (diplomats and families and  others) who are being air-
evaculted form Wuhan.   They are on a plane from China to Alaska to California.  
Concern about whethernor not to quarantine them for 14 days when we did not and do 
not quarantine Chinese who pass screening on entry.   Marty Cetron had argued that the 
American were very recently in the “hot zone” whereas the chines who are coming in 
now are not really coming from Wuhan since Wuhan has been shut down by the Chinese.  
Also, political concern of what it looks like to quarantine or “imprision” US citizen 
versus what happens if we let them in and they start infecting people.   Finally decide to 
do a sft verion of bringin them in to a military airbase – the March Air reserve Base in 
Riverside County. CA, and consider them all not a low risk.   They are either medium or 
high risk based on their exposure.   They all will be tested (nasal swab PCR) and detained 
at the base for up to 72 hours until the tests come back and then released.   The “high” 
risk people majr get more intense investigation Discussed for hours in the Situation 
Room.  The meeting was chaired by Mick Mulvaney and most Deputies were present 
together with Matt Pottinger, Kellyanne Conway, Ken Cucinelli, Dr. Navarro, Biegun, 
Blair, Eisenberg, Szabat, Lidell, Foret (CBP)John Wilson, John Mark (?).
Chinese scientists are saying that the epidemic is much worse than is being reported.   Dr. 
Yuan say that 50% of the infections are asymptomatic.   However, this is confusing 
people since he does not say what percent of these are spreading while asymptomatic.   A 
lot of confusion and misinformation while the outbreak accelerates.
Azar wanted the POTUS to be briefed by me in the Oval office after the Sit Room, but a 
fluke prevented this.   Brian Harrison called me into a side room for a few questions and 
Azar was looking for me and could not find me and so he and Redfield went to the Oval 
without me.   Innocent screwup.
Press conference with Azar – multiple media reporting with several clips of me; Lou 
Dobbs FOX; Marc Siegal FOX; CBS This Morning;

entries.content:
Got a call this AM from Lou Dobbs who told me that President Trump
will be calling me.  Lou spoke with the POTUS andf told him that I was the “smartest 
person” around  and he should speak with me.
Amazing day today!  
Bob Kadlec, Bob Redfield, Karin King (State), Ken Cuccinelli (DHS), Jonathan Fritz 
(State) briefed the House members led by Nancy Pelosi who was her usual self with me 
(big hug, kiss and telling everyone how great I am -  little embarrassing.   Diane DeGette 
did the same thing.
At the Deputies Meeting in the Situation Room (4:00 to 5:15 PM) – big surprise.   Mick 
Mulvaney led the meeting and after about 1 hour the President came in and the first 
thing he said as he looked at me was: “Anthony, you are really a famous guy.   My good 
friend Lou Dobbs (see above) told me that you were the one of the smartest, 
knowledgeable and outstanding persons he knows.   He then stayed for 20 minutes and 
asked most of his questions of me.  I was surprised and very pleased and the Deputies 
were clearly stunned and impressed.   When Trump finally left, he said: “Anthony, are we 
OK?”   I said: “We are good”.   He smiled and as he walked out of the room, he said 
“Thanks, again, Anthony.   We are counting on you”. 
The arrival of the US passengers at March base was a total success.  They arrived on a 
Kalitta Air Boeing 747.(NPR)   The passenegers were extatic to be home.   The real issue 
now is how do we get out the 200,000 US citizens who are in China if they want to leave.   
It will be a logistical challenge.
Cases 7700 with 170 deaths
Clips of HHS press conference showing on different TV networks; NPR “On Point”;

Another amazing and difficult day.  Briefed the House Energy and
Commerce Committee members in Rayburn 2123.   All my friends kept saying I was a 
national hero and they “….felt safe in my arms (Eschoo)”.   Testifying with me were Bob 
redfield, Bob Kadlec and denise Hinton (FDA).
The chaos:   We had 2 PCCS led by Ruggiero and one Deputies lead by Mick Mulvaney 
with the usal cast of characters.   Case in point.  Mart Cetron who was listening in on the 
WHO call said that the epidemic was accelerating that this is was clear that the 
incubation period was shorter (2-5 days than was previously felt and that asymptomatic 
transmission was occurring.   Thus, it was agreed to present to the POTUS a revised plan 
for containment:   The 200 people at March Base would be quarantines for 15 days.   
Anyone coming in from Wuhan would be quarantined for 15 days.   Anyone from any 
part of China would be voluntarily isolated for 15 days with monitoring by public health 
officials (State/Local).      Azar would declare a Public Health Emergency and the State 
Department level alert would be level 4.
The number of cases today are: 9480 with 213 deaths.   It is increasing by about 25% per 
day.   In 1 month it has surpassed SARS for 1 year (8000).
WHO Declares a PHEIC
Politico (Dan Diamond) is coming out with an article bashing badly Azar.   HHS COMS 
had me speak to Dan and I greatly praised Azar.
The POTUS announced the Coronavirus Task Force today (see below):
Members of the President’s Coronavirus Task Force:
Secretary Alex Azar, Department of Health and Human Services
Robert O’Brien, Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs
Dr. Robert Redfield, Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
Dr. Anthony Fauci, Director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases 
at the National Institutes of Health
Deputy Secretary Stephen Biegun, Department of State
Ken Cuccinelli, Acting Deputy Secretary, Department of Homeland Security
Joel Szabat, Acting Under Secretary for Policy, Department of Transportation
Matthew Pottinger, Assistant to the President and Deputy National Security Advisor
Rob Blair, Assistant to the President and Senior Advisor to the Chief of Staff
Joseph Grogan, Assistant to the President and Director of the Domestic Policy Council
Christopher Liddell, Assistant to the President and Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy 
Coordination
Derek Kan, Executive Associate Director, Office of Management and Budget
PRESS: FOX – “Fox and Friends”; ABC TV local; NBC TV local; PBS NewsHour; 
WTOP radio X2

Another truly amazing day.   Sequested in the White House essentially
all day working out a proposal to put before the POTUS that would restrict travel from 
China.  The proposal was driven largely by CDC (Marty Cetron) who felt that given the 
volume of people coning in from China by direct and even more importantly indirect 
flights it would be logistically impossible to effectively screen people at many, many 
airports and the diversion of people from their place of origin to selective airports would 
further complicate things.   Also, the cases continue to sharply rise with 12000 cases and 
259 deaths.   Also, a NEJM report from Germany indicated that a Chinese woman came 
from Shanghai visited a colleague in Stockdorf Bavaria.  She infected him when she had 
no sxs, returned to China and got sik on the plane.  The german man then got sick and 
infected 2 other Germans.   This would have bn the first truly documented case of 
transmission from an asymptomatic person, thus, adding to the concern about the 
accuracy of screening at airports.  In addition, the WHO declared a PHEIC yesterday 
prompting Azar to declare a Public Health Emergency here in the USA.   I disagreed with 
the latter since there were only 7 infections (6 travel) at the time.   All this led to the 
conclusion of travel restriction.   This was late in the afternoon  - around 1:30-2:00 PM.   
The entire task force (above) plus Kellyanne Conway, Jessica Zitto (WH Coms) and a 
variety oof senior WH officials gatherd in the Roosevelt Room to hammer out how we 
would present this to the POTUS.   The policy decision was:  1) Ban travel to the USA of 
all non-citizens who have been to China within the past 14 days.   If you were in China, 
you need to go somewhere else (Paris, UK, etc.) until 14 days pass from the time you 
were in China. 2) If you are a citizen and were in the Hubei Province (includes Wuhan) 
and you return to USA, you are institutionally quarantined for 14 days. 3) If you come 
from any other part of China other than Hubei, you have voluntary isolation for 14 days.
We wanted to present this to the POTUS befor the Stock Market closed so that we do not 
look like we held off to avoid bad effects.   We went into the Oval Office at about 3:00 
PM.   We had been scheduled to go in at 2:30 PM but things backed up.  Presentation was 
made to the POTUS by Azar, Bob Redfield and me.   Trump as he did a couple of ddays 
ago posed many questions to me making sure that I thought it was a good idea.   I said 
this was an imperfect process, but the best choice we have right now.   He questioned me 
about what the difference was between this and flu.   He somewhat brashly suggested 
even more stringent restrictions and was dyswaded by Kellyanne.   She clearly has 
influence over the POTUS.
Potus agreed and we immediately went out to the WH Press Briefing room that was 
packed.   Azar led the presentation, but many questions were ansered by me.   Interesting 
that impeachment was going on and the senate did not get the 4 GOP votes to allow 
witnesses to be called.   This also dominated the news.   We thought this would get us on 
the Sunday Talk Shows, but impeachment bumped us.  White House is now fully 
convinced that I be the science/health spokesperson for the USG.   Bob Redfield just does 
not come across very weel.   He takes forever to say something and it is usually 
wondering.   This drives the WH and HHS comms people crazy and so they are putting 
me out on all the requests.
When I got back to my office, got call from Jeremy Farrar who sounded very concerned 
and conferenced me in with Kristian Anderson, an evolutionary biologist from Scripps.  
They had also been talking with Eddie Holmes, another evolutionary biologistfrom 
Sidney Australia.   There have been conspiracy theories that the virus was given GOF by 
inserted mutations and deliberately or accidentally released in Wuhan.   One theory was 
written by Indian investigators that HIV sequences were inserted by a Chinese person in 
Canada and released in Wuhan.   Everyone thinks that is crazy, but the Farrar phone call 
was different.   The people on the phone felt that the mutations around the furine 
cleavage site of the spike protein could not have occurred naturally since it would require 
an evolutionary “jump that they found nowhere in bat isolates.   They bring up the 
possibility that this could have been deliberately inserted and either accidentally released 
or deliberately released by a crazy person in the lab, the former being the most likely.   
Jeremy was calling me for advice.   I suggest that we get a larger group of qualified 
evolutionary biologists/virologists together under the auspices of a convening body and 
carefully look at this.  We agreed to convene by phone the next day.   I called Brian 
Harrison and Garrett Grigsby who arranged for a call with Azar to decide what to do.   
Azar did not like the idea of WHO as convener because he feels (somewhat unfairly, I 
believe) that Tedros would immediately tell the Chinese and they would crush the 
attempt and/or think we are attacking them.   We decided to have a 2-pronged approach 
strongly suggested by Kadlec who felt we had security responsibilities to investigate this 
ourselves.  He would do this through OSTP and NAS.   Meanwhile I would pursue a 
multinational approach with Jeremy.   I decided to now bring in Francis.
PRESS: The Today Show NBC; Lou Dobbs Fox; many print
Feb. 1, 2020 -  Conference call at 2:00 PM with Jeremy, Francis and several other 
scientists gathered by Jeremy (see below).
Participants in the Feb., 2020 call included:
• Francis Collins, Director of the U.S. National Institutes of Health, U.S.;
• Anthony Fauci, Director of the U.S. National Institute of Allergy and Infectious 
Diseases, U.S.;
• Jeremy Farrar, Director of the Wellcome Trust;

There was not total agreement about the likelihood of deliberate insertion.   Ron Fouchier 
said he was sure that this could occur naturally and we should not waste our time and 
divert effort to pursue this.   This is expected of him since he was the original GOF 
person with Yoshi Kawaoka.   Also, Christian Drosten was with Ron; the rest felt that 
deliberate insertion was possible and given the fact that Dr. Zheng-Li Shi  at the 
University of Wuhan has been working for years in GOF in coronaviruses to allow 
adaptation of the spike protein to bind to the human ACE2 receptor, we could not let this 
go.  We decided to have Jeremy with Francis to contact Tedros with Stewart Simonson’s 
help (I arranged this) to see if Tedros would convene experts.
Meanwhile, the DHS and DOT and FAA are working hard on the logistics of diverting 
plans to selected airports that are associated with the capability of screening with 
questions and quarantining or moving to voluntary isolation.
Airports are: LAX, SFO, Seattle, ATL, ORD, Hawaii, Newark, IAD, Detroit, DFW
JFK, and Seattle
PRESS:  CNN (truck came to my house since I was so busy with wall-to-wall 
conference calls and hundreds of e-mails.;

Call from Sylvia Burwell asking for clarification of the new policy
regarding AU students who are returning fom China.   Apparently, the policy is not up on 
the CDC website.
Had daily Task Force call.  Discussed the difficult logistics of airport funneling and 
quarantine/isolation at land crossings with Canada and Mexico.
Cases now 14,551 and 304 deaths
Now 3 aditional cases in USA = 11
Kansas City Chiefs beat SF  49ers – Patrick Mahomes stars abd comes back from 10 
point deficit in the 4th quarter.
PRESS:  MSNBC; Fox Local TV; NBC Nightly News; CNN with Anna Cabrera

Task Force meeting daily.    Repatriated people from Wuhan 150 tested
negative; no positives thus far.  Cases = 17,205 with 361 deaths; 26 countries have 180 
international cases and within that there are 20 human to human transmission 
transmissions with no sustained transmission yet.
Complicated issue with border crossings of Chinese at Canada and Mexico. Many come 
over, but screening capabilities are not like we have at airport.
Travis AFB, Miramar, Lackland AFB are landing destinations for US Citizens coming 
from Wuhan so that we can implememnt institutional quarantines and medical care if 
needed.
Spoke with George Gao tonight in China.   George is the Director General of the Chinese 
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.   He confirmed that infected people can be 
asymptomatic and that asymptomatic people can transmit.   This is important since the 
recent NEJM paper that said that a Chinese woman who went from Shanghai to Germany 
and infected a business associate while she was asymptomatic was in fact mildly 
symptomatic and so the NEJM paper is incorrect.   However, the fact is still true.   Also, 
George was very sensitive and understandably defensive since he was the one who said 
early on that there was no human to human transmission and that the original 27 cases in 
the wet market reported on December 31, 2019 were animal to human when actually 
human to human transmission was occurring weeks before.   The Wuhan health officials 
did not tell him this and he thus gave out false information.   This lapse likely allowed the 
outbreak to take hold since Wuhan went about their business with 40,000 pot luck 
festivals without social distancing.
Failure of HIV vaccine trial HVTN-702 (Uhambo) conducted in South Africa  >5000 
participants showed no efficacy at all.   DSMB stopped trial due to futility
PRESS:  WTOP Radio; CNBC; TRT Turkish TV (x2); CGTN Chinese TV; On 
camera interview with Jennifer Ashton in VRC – ABC News; Lou Dobbs FOX 
News.

entries.content:
20,680 cases and 27 deaths.   No sign of diminishing.   We are hearing the
obvious conflicting opinions of the benefit or harm of travel restrictions.
A lot of interest in the revealing that the NEJM paper claiming in one Chinese to German 
transmission that it was symptomatic transmission, when it probably was not.   I quoted 
that paper (now flawed) in the WH presser.
One death in Hong Kong (total of 2 with Phillippines for non-China deaths)
20,680/426 – 2% mortality
Continuing to evacuate USC from Wuhan.   4 individuals from Hubei Province under 
quarantine (2 LAX, 1 ORD, 1 NY)
Chinese officials criticizing USA for travel restrictions.  WHO also adding muted 
criticism.
Got urgent e-mail from Lindsey Baden from NEJM to review in 2 hours a pape from 
Germany showing that an asymptomatic person can harbor replication competent virus in 
nasal passages.
State of the Union address tonight and vote on conviction after impeachment tomorrow – 
weird!
PRESS:  Bloomberg Radio;Vox print; Marc Siegal Doctor Radio – Sirius; NPR – 
“All Things Considered”- Richard Harris; Good Morning America – ABC;  Yahoo 
Finance TV; NY Times – Roni Caryn Rabin; Reuters print; Israeli TV – i24 LIVE; 
Picture in Washington Post; BBC Radio interview

Spenty the day on the Hill as part of the President’s Coronavirus Task
Force led by Alex Azar and Mick Mulvany to brief first the Senators in the Dirksen 
Building led by Lamar Alexander and Patty Murray and then the House led by Rosa 
DeLauro and Tom Cole in the Capitol Visitor’s Center.  Also, spent time in the SCIF 
planning for tomorrow when we may be briefing the POTUS again.
25,000 cases/479 deaths.
President was acquitted today by the Senate on a partisan vote.
Much print press about every aspect of nCoV, particularly the controversy about 
asymptomatic transmission. In the Washington Post today, Nancy Pelosi, when asked 
whether she feels the administration is doing a good job, said the following:
Post – Feb. 5, 2020:
Exiting the briefing, House Speaker Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.) praised Anthony 
Fauci, director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases who is 
also on the administration task force, saying she had worked with him for years. 
Fauci was among those briefing lawmakers on Wednesday.
“He has confidence in what is happening at CDC, so again, my confidence is in 
him,” Pelosi said. “I think we have to be appropriately alert but not 
fearmongering on this, and I think that’s the right tempo.”
Asked about Azar’s leadership, Pelosi said: “I don’t know that much about Azar 
but I know Fauci. All I know about Azar is he used to work for a pharmaceutical 
company. I don’t know that much about his experience with disease but Dr. Fauci 
is a doctor, and this is his life’s work.”
Tragic news – Eric Scorce (my nephew) found dead in his apartment.   Likely 
sudden heart attack.
PRESS:  KCBS Radio – San Francisco; MSNBC; Radio Free Asia (TV); Wed MD; 
Washington Post

entries.content:
Cases continue to soare with 28,018/563.  Another packed day mostly at
HHS and White House.   Conspiracy theories still abound.   The NAS group with OSTP 
met (see above) and decided that there was no clear evidence of malfeasance, but it 
should be looked into (see attachement below):
NASEM Response 
to OSTP re Coronavi   
Briefed the Asia/East Asia Ambassadors on nCoV in Room EEOB-350. Then had long 
meeting of Coronavirus Task Force is Sit Room of WH chaired by Mick Mulvany at 
4:00- 4:45PM when the core group of Task Force were called to Oval Office to brief 
POTUS.   When we walked in the POTUS was not yet in the room.   When he walked in 
with Melania, the first thing he did was say“"Anthony, come here and say hello to 
Melania”.   Then, to my embarrassment in front of everyone (Kellyanne, Mick, Bob 
O’Brien and many in Cabinet) he told Melania that I was the smartest person in the 
world.   We then sat down and briefed him and Melania.  He asked what he could do and 
we said that since he would be calling Chinese President Xi Jinping late this evening, he 
could ask him to approve the WHO delegation of scientists that include CDC and NIH 
people.   He did what he did last time and directed most of the questions to me, again 
ending with asking me if I thought that we were on the right track.
During the task Force meeting, the issues came up of cruise ships (one in Yokohama, 
Japan, and one in New Jersey/New York) that had infected Chinese from Wuhan on them 
and discussion of how to handle quarantine for the rest of the passengers. 
PRESS: India TV; Podcast with Newt Gingrich; Podcast with Howard Buchner at 
JAMA (well-received by NYT and WSJ reporters.
Feb. 7, 2020 – Started with 7:00 AM with a multi-party call hosted by WHO.  Got good 
information. See below.
31,211/637.  61 infections on Japanese cruise ship. Chinese are starting to see a slight 
downtrend in cases.   Perhaps we are turning things around in China?   I warn on the call 
that we need to give developing countries the resources to do contact tracing and isolation 
or else as we decrease China, another country will become like China.   Also, need 
serologies to determine extent of asymptomatic and minimally symptomatic infection so 
that we can determine the true case fatality rate among other things.
Cancelled trip to Florida for Chris’s birthday.  So sorry.
PRESS: Press conference at HHS with Azar, Redfield, Cuccinnelli, Biegun, Szabat; 
CNN; interviewed with: USA Today,   Bloomberg Law (Jeannie Beaumann), 
Arizona republic, NY Times (Denise Grady), Bloomberg News (Bob Langreth; 
WJLA TV ABC7 (Local); CNN with Lou Dobbs.

Numbers today: 34,867/724.  First USCit died in Wuhan.   Much press
about this and the cruise ships in Japan and Bayonne.   Infections and quarantine of the 
Japan ship (61 so far, including some USCits.  10 people under quarantine from airport 
screening at the 11 airports.   People on Japanese ship getting cabin fever with 
quarantine.  People on Bayonne ship have all been released and the Chinese nationals on 
the ship are going home.
Tom Frieden called me this AM and we discussed various aspects of the outbreak.   He 
and I are on the same page in thinking tht this is acting like a bad influenza in its 
transmissibility and that the denominator is much greater than 34,867 (above) making the 
case fatality rate (CFR) more like 0.2-0.3 % rather than 2.0%.
PRESS:  FOX and Friends; WTOP Radio; MSNBC

Sunday, but it goes on.   37,593/814.   People on the Japanese cruise ship
are being released from quarantine.  Outbreak still raging in China.   Still only 12 cases in 
USA (9 travel from Wuhan and 2 spouses of 2 of the 9).
Briefed the Governors at the Governors convention at the DC Convention Center
PRESS:  CNN International (good interview)

40,625/910.   Outbreak still progressing.  I will list below the quarantine
centers associated with the various funneled airports:
JB Pearl Harbor-Hickam, Hawaii (HNL)
Great Lakes Training Center Navy Base, Illinois (ORD)
Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base, Texas (DFW)
March ARB, California (LAX)
Travis AFB, California (SFO)
Dobbins ARB, Georgia (ATL)
Fort Hamilton, New York (JFK)
Naval Base Kitsap, Washington (SEA)
Joint Base Anacostia, Washington DC (IAD)
Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst, New Jersey (EWR)
Fort Custer Training Center, Michigan (DTW)
The Department of Defense already has quarantine centers at Fort Carson in 
Colorado, Travis Air Force Base and Marine Corps Air Station Miramar in 
California, and Lackland Air Force Base in Texas.
Ken Cucinnelli sends e-mail to Task Force saying that we should be much more 
aggressive in “mitigation” right now and not wait until outbreak in USA occurs.  
This triggers calls at HHS since it might look like HHS is not doing things 
correctly.   Had a vigorous Task Force call at 4:00 PM to discuss merssaging and 
the fact that we need to prepare for mitigation.   Ken Cuccinelli wants to prepare 
families and businesses to how they would respond to an outbreak.   I pushed back 
saying that my experience with anthrax and the “duct tape” incident made me feel 
that this would inspire unnecessary panic or ridicule.   We should prepare more 
forward-looking at the state and local health levels, not the family level.
Infections on the Japanese Cruise ship up to 136.   Sick people taken off and rest 
quarantined on ship.   Question raised whether aerosol spread through ventilation 
system similar to spread of SARS in 2004 in Amoy Garden Apartment Complex 
in Hong Kong.
97 people die in China yesterday – most for a single day.
CDC wants the airlines give them the contact information of passangers so that 
they can be tracked.
Bob Redfield having trouble clearly articulating the process of converting from 
containment to mitigation.   He is a good guy, but Bob is Bob.   Azar/HHS/and 
WH are all putting me out there to explain things within our group and to the 
press.   Bob seems OK and modestly wants to learn.   I like him.
PRESS: CNN (Jim Sciutto); Diane Rehm Podcast; Sean Hannity Radio Show; 
CNN International.

13th American infected (San Diego).   One of the people air-
evacuated by State to Miramar from Wuhan.   Minimal sxs.
43,138/1018
Bob Kadlec offers the Japanese help in providing remdesivir in a compassionate 
use protocol to the people on the Diamond Princess cruise ship in Yokohama.   
Now 131 people infected and the rest are quarantined.   I offer Cliff Lane to help 
with the protocol.
A PCC document that I just read is proposing that even in Phase IV (see below) 
we should continue INA 212 (f) travel restrictions.   I disagree with this since 
travel restrictions are to delay the entry of disease into your country.   Once you 
have sustained transmission in your country, it is a waste of resources to try to 
keep out travelers.   I cannot be on the PCC call this AM (on a panel at the Aspen 
Institute in DC) and so I called Bob Redfield and asked him to respresent me and 
my reservations about this:
Phases of U.S. Government Response to the 2019 Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV)
Phase I—Current Posture
• Description: Foreign nationals who have been in China within 14 days prior to their 
actual or attempted entry into the United States are ineligible for admission under 
Section 212 (f) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA).  Departments and 
agencies may exercise certain exemptions.  Any person, but specifically U.S. 
citizens and legal permanent residents (LPRs) who have been: (1) in Hubei 
province within the past 14 days may be subject to 14 day mandatory quarantine; 
and (2) in China (outside Hubei province) within the past 14 days may be subject 
to screening and self-isolation for 14 days.  All direct and indirect flights from 
China are funneled to 11 airports with enhanced CDC medical screening.  CDC is 
coordinating with state and local health care clinicians to identify domestic cases, 
isolate cases, and conduct appropriate contact tracing.
o Triggers: Already being implemented.
• Objectives: (1) Contain the outbreak at its source, (2) minimize domestic 
importation of additional cases, (3) limit potential for domestic epidemic, and (4) 
prepare the domestic response mechanisms.
• Messaging: Daily HHS and CDC briefings and on camera task force briefings as 
appropriate.
Phase II—Aggressive Containment
• Description: Expand the scope of the travel ban to account for additional states or 
territories.  Apply quarantine measures above to people not covered by the travel 
ban, including U.S. persons, but who have traveled to these additional states or 
territories within the time frames described above.  All direct and indirect flights 
from these additional states or territories will be funneled to the 11 airports with 
enhanced CDC medical screening.  Consider reducing the number of airports to 
concentrate screening resources. CDC further coordinates with state and local 
health care clinicians to identify domestic cases, isolate cases, and conduct 
appropriate contact tracing.
o Triggers: Sustained human to human transmission and exportation of cases 
without nexus to China.
• Objectives: (1) Limit the outbreak to the source and additional outbreak areas, (2) 
minimize importation of additional cases, (3) limit potential for domestic epidemic, 
(4) additional preparation of the domestic response mechanisms and in some cases 
executing those plans, and (5) begin outreach to state and local authorities to 
prepare for Phase III and Phase IV.
• Messaging: XYZ.
• Specific Department and Agency Activities: XYZ.
Phase III—Partial Mitigation
• Description: Travel restrictions put in place by active INA 212(f) proclamations 
remain in place.  Those not covered by any active travel bans, including U.S. 
persons from identified countries are allowed to travel to their final destination and 
may then be subject to self-isolation for 14 days, as coordinated by state and local 
authorities.  Individuals who travel to the affected domestic areas or live in those 
areas may be subject to self-isolation for 14 days, as coordinated by state and local 
authorities.  
o Triggers: Sustained human to human transmission without nexus to China 
in two or more domestic locations.
• Objectives: (1) Implement the national response, (2) reacting to the first domestic 
epicenters, and (3) mitigating and minimizing the impact of the disease.
• Messaging: XYZ.
• Specific Department and Agency Activities: XYZ.
Phase IV—Mitigation
• Description: Travel restrictions put in place by active INA 212(f) proclamations 
remain in place.  Limit non-essential domestic travel, cancel public gatherings, 
social distancing, execute private sector and government continuity of operations.
o Triggers: Wide-spread domestic human to human transmission, could be in 
cities or regional.
• Objectives: (1) Preserve the functioning of critical infrastructure and mitigate 
impact to the economy and functioning of society, and (2) support community 
responses to the extent possible to mitigate illness, suffering, and death.
• Messaging: XYZ.
• Specific Department and Agency Activities: XYZ.
WHO officially names the 2019-nCoV as “COVID19”.   Was on Panel at Aspen Institute 
chaired by Helen Branswell and with Nancy Messonnier and Ron Klain as co-panelists.   
Reminisced with Ron about the Ebole-White House days
PRESS:  NPR Radio 1A (Todd Zwillick); WTOP Radio; Press at the Aspen 
Institute (2300 N Street); FOX News (Lou Dobbs)

45,172/1115  Individual reports are coming out about various
clinical characteristics.   Unreviewed report now of virus in saliva of infected 
people.   Let us see what kind of reponse that gets.
Very busy day today with 4 Congressionald briefings!   Also, complicated by 
wake of Eric Scorce today and funeral tomorrow.   Much stress.
First we briefed House members at Rayburn led by Rosa DeLauro, Nita Lowey 
and Tom Cole.   Then we went to the Senate Dirksen to brief senators led by 
Lamar Alexander.   Then to Capitol Visitors center to brief House members led by 
Eliot Engel.   Then to Majority hosue leader Steny Hoyer’s office to brief 
members.   Steny was profuse in his praise for me, which was  a little 
embarrassing
On my way out of White House from the 4:00 to 5:00 PM Task Force meeting, ran 
into Larry Kudlow, who has become my new best friend.   He joked about how 
many years I have been doing this and he has been following my career.   His 
main question was when is this COVID19 going to crash the economy, i.e. when 
does he need to start worrying about it.   It told him that we are OK for now but 
this could change rapidly if we start seing sustained person-to-person 
transmission.   He asked me to keep him informed when in my opinion things are 
starting to go bad 
Having our second big multipeson conference call this AM with Mike Ryan, 
Tedros and WHO, Bruce Aylward (Canadian) called from China.  He is part of 
WHO multi-national advance team in China.  Still no invitation for US 
representation from China to be part of group. Azar getting very angry and 
blaming Tedros for not pushing with China to get us on the group.  Azar feels that 
Tedros in bowing to Xi Jinping who does not want USA.  Tough situation since 
Tedros and WHO depends greatly on China and often bows to them.
PRESS:  WTOP Radio; Bloomberg TV (by phone;

60,349/1369    Sharp increase in that they are not using just lab
test for DX; they are using chest x-rays and CT scans of lung.
Meeting at White House with Chairs and Ranking members of big 4 committees 
with  Anne Schuket, General Paul Friedrichs, Bob Kadlec in Roosevelt Room.  
Kevin McCarthy, Steve Scalise, Greg Walden.   Chaired by Mick Mulvaney.   
Also, Eric Ueland of WH Lewg there.   Good questions.   Many compliments
PRESS:  CBS This Morning (for showing tomorrow); FOX News (Lou 
Dobbs)

64,460/1384   Making plans to deal with Americans on Princess
Diamond Cruise ship in Yokohama harbor.   Cliff flying to Japan to help design a 
clinical trial to treat infected people with remdesivir.   Then he is off to China as 
part of the WHO-sponsored delegation.
Azar, Redfield, Kadlec and I briefed the entire Cabinet on a teleconference this 
AM
PRESS:  FOX  Business; Spectrum News TV; Fox News with Dana 
perino;CBS This Morning ; CNBC

67,178/1527.  Had White House Task Force conference call at
12:00 noon (Saturday).   Big issue was the plan to get Americans off the Diamond 
Princess in Yokohama harbor.   State will charter planes to get them to Lackland 
and Travis AF bases.   Sick people will stay in Japanese hospitals.   Uninfected 
and people whoise status is not clear will be flown out with the proper PPE for 
those who are thought to be at roisk of being infected.
Also, discussed on the call the persistent problem of cruise ships in general, which 
could derail all polasn for containment since they scatter people from all over the 
world to all over the world.
Important conference call chaired by Bob Kadlec with the ASPR and CDC people 
who are on the ground with the Diamond Princess Cruise ship in Yokohama.  The 
conditions apper to be dreadful with major transmission on the boat.   Many crew 
members getting infected.   Japanese are not adhering to the required PPE.  It 
seems that they are unaware of the potential transmissibility of the virus.  The 
CDC people say the ship is like an “incubator” for the virus.   One called it a 
cesspool of virus.  This conversation makes it clear that we need to get US citizens 
off that ship.  James Lawlor (Nebraska) and Michael Callahan (Mass. General) 
were on the call.
PRESS:  FOX News with Molly Line;

69,275/1670  (Sunday)  Big discussion on phone with Kadlec,
Anne Schuchat and Kevin (ASPR) on whether to remove a person from the 
evacuation plane who recently showed to be positive.  Original plan was that 
anyone who was infected would not board plane evacuating people from the 
Diamond Princess.  Now Kadlec and Kevin want to board them since people on 
the bus waiting to board have already been exposed on the bus to several people 
who are infected.
Washington Post story by Jasmeen Abutaleb has me defending Azar against slurs 
against him (covertly by administration officials).   I also say that w need to be fair 
to the POTUS (see below):
"In fairness to the president, someone told him something that has a basis in 
reality. ... There is some validity in saying respiratory viruses like flu and 
coronavirus are seasonal," Fauci said. "The only thing is when you're dealing 
with a pandemic-type virus that is brand new, there's no way of knowing what's 
going to happen when the weather gets warm."
Some officials have complained that Trump's comments about the virus emanate 
from his briefings with Azar, who they say has been overly controlling in the 
response and has told other doctors not to get too far into the details of the virus 
and the outbreak with Trump. Azar is disliked by many in the White House, four 
administration officials say.
Fauci, however, said Azar has brought medical professionals with him to nearly 
every briefing and insisted they be part of Oval Office meetings.
Azar "always defers to the scientists. That's the reason why whenever we're in 
the Situation room and the president would like some briefing, Alex always takes 
me and (CDC director) Bob Redfield in with him," Fauci said. "He always wants 
us to give the straight scientific information to the president."
PRESS: Face the Nation (Margaret Brennan);

71,438/1775.   454 infected on Diamond Princess cruise ship.
Heated discussion last evening (see above) with Bob Kadlec, Will Walters (State 
Med), Anne Schuchat, Kevin (ASPR) about whether to board people on the 
evacuation 747 plane who were originally scheduled to come home as 
“uninfected” after they just found out that 14 of them are in fact infected.   The 
written agreement is that no documented infected people should get on the evac 
plane.   Walters, Kevin and to some extent Bob Kadlec (he was complicit) insisted 
that since they were already on the bus, we should allow them on the plane.  They 
said that we would not know what to do with them if they stayed since we could 
not leave them on the ship and the Japanese did not have facilities to take care of 
them (I do not believe the latter).  Anne Schuchat vehemently argued that they 
should not be allowed to board since the public and written agreement was that 
they would be put on a plane WITHOUT infected people and this would be 
breaking that agreement.   Nonetheless, Walters pushed and Kadlec (ASPR) caved 
and went along.   Of note, later on (today) Walters said that he checked with me 
and I was OK with the boarding – a lie!   On the call today Azar was upset since 
the entire Cabinet was questioning why we let them board and when he asked our 
stance, he heard that we (HHS) disagreed.   He was upset that we did not speak 
with one voice and this looked bad.   On the call today, I told him that State 
(Walters) was going to do what he wanted to do anyway no matter what we said.   
Of note, on these issues in foreign countries, State has the last word.
Several of the 14 infected people from ship who were evacuated went to Nebraska.  
Also 3 additional people were notified while on the plane that they were infected.   
We air evacuated 328 people from Diamond Princess.  61 Americans elected to 
stay in Japan on the ship, but the Japanese want them off the ship because 
transmission is occurring on the ship.  There are now 800+ non-China cases, 365 
of which are on Diamond Princess.   Now 28 countries have cases and within these 
there are 183 human to human transmissions.   Singapore is problem with 68% of 
their cases are human to human
PRESS: WTOP Radio; FOX (Caputo) TV; FOX Business TV; CNN (Wolf 
Blitzer Situation Room).

73,335/1876.  More infections appearing on Diamond Princess.
Good thing we got our people off the ship.
Director of a major Wuhan hospital dies of COVID-19. Liu Zhiming, 51yo 
neurologist 
Did panel at the Council on Foreign Relations chaired by Fran Townsend.  Bob 
Kadlec was other panelist.
Much discussion about Cruise ship issues.
Our planes land in Lakeland and Travis with evacuated Americans.   Infected 
people shipped to University of Nebraska for containment; remainder of the 
uninfected go into 14 day quarantine
PRESS: CNN New Day (Jim Sciutto and Alisyn Camerota); BBC Radio; 
CNN International; FOX America Newsroom; CNBC; FOX News (Laura 
Ingraham)

75,201/2012.  On WHO weekly call with Mike Ryan. 1700 health
care workers have been infected.  Starting to discuss the role of environmental 
(surfaces) spread of virus, particularly in the context of the Diamond Princess.  
Mike Ryan makes good point that the stringent control efforts of China are putting 
pressure on the virus not to spread.  This is somewhat artificial.   He is concerned 
that the virus in other countries that cannot be so draconian in control we might 
see a resurgence of the virus that is being artificially controlled in China.
CDC Comms concerned that I am being too hard on the Japanese by sayng 
publicly that their quarantine failed.   They contacted Courtney.   Too bad.  I tell it 
like it is.   They completely messed up the infection control on the Diamond 
Princess.   They had over 500 people infected on the ship.  Problem is that 
Japanese are releasing people into the community from the ship without the 
complete 14 day quarantine.   They consider being on the ship as quarantine when 
it is not.  We have “do not board” orders on the people who have left the ship until 
they are off the ship for 14 days.
PRESS:  NPR “Morning Edition”; KCBS Radio (San Francisco); FOX 
Business News; Siriusx Radio – Michael Smerconish; Nextstar TV; Wall 
Street Journal Pocast; NBC Nightly News (did not show – may show in AM); 
PBS NewsHour (William Brangham); FOX News (Lou Dobbs)

75,752/2130.  Had major discussions last evening among the HHS
team.   Some disagreement that we had to sort out between ASPR (Kadlec) and 
CDC (Cetron/Redfield) regarding when to trigger the transition from containment 
to mitigation.   Kadlec wanted to do it if only 1 location (city, etc) had more than 3 
rounds of transmission, whereas CDC wanted to trigger to be >3 rounds in more 
than one non-contiguous location (city, etc.) .   After much conference call 
discussion we came to a compromise.
Azar pissed off at a story in the Washington Post by Lena Sun.   Someone leaked 
the story about the disagreement between CDC and State/ASPR regarding 
allowing infected Americans to board the evacuation plane taking people from the 
Diamond Princess back to the USA.   Now this is a big story:  “Infected patients 
put on plane against CDC advice”
PRESS:  Radio Free Asia (TV); The Doctors TV Show; Home Care Radio 
(HCR); NBC Nightly News (from yesterday)

76,775/2247.   1st patient to die from being on Diamond Princess.
Had intense “Table Top”=like exercise with the WHTF in the Situation Room 
from 3:00to 5:00 PM.   Discussed the plans and triggers of going from 
containment to mitigation.   Lots of good discussion.   Led by Mick Mulvaney.

Dr. Anthony Fauci, director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, 
speaking before the House Appropriations Committee on Wednesday.Credit...Anna 
Moneymaker/The New York Times
By 
Denise Grady
• March 8, 2020, 3:04 p.m. ET
•  •  Dr. Anthony Fauci, the nation’s leading expert on infectious diseases, is widely 
respected for his ability to explain science without talking down to his audience — and 
lately, for managing to correct the president’s pronouncements without saying he is 
wrong.
President Trump said that drug companies would make a coronavirus vaccine ready 
“soon.” Dr. Fauci has repeatedly stepped up after the president to the lectern during 
televised briefings or at White House round tables to amend that timetable, giving a more 
accurate estimate of at least a year or 18 months.
Mr. Trump said a “cure” might be possible. Dr. Fauci explained that antiviral drugs were 
being studied to see if they might make the illness less severe. The president also said the 
disease would go away in the spring. Dr. Fauci said maybe so, but because it was caused 
by a new virus, there was no way to tell.
Experts like Dr. Fauci should be the ones who speak to the public during epidemics, said 
Representative Donna E. Shalala of Florida, who was his boss during the Obama 
administration, when she led the Department of Health and Human Services.
“I think Tony is playing the same exact role that he has in the past — to make sure the 
science is accurate and clear,” Ms. Shalala said. “During a health emergency, it’s the 
scientists and physicians that are the credible people to the American public, not 
politicians.”
“I used to make him wear his white coat when talking to the public,” she added. “I used 
to make them all wear their white coats so people were reassured that they are real 
doctors.”
On Sunday, Dr. Fauci appeared on at least two television news shows, warning that as the 
virus spread — there were more than 450 cases in at least 33 states — some stricter 
measures to isolate the infected might be considered. He also offered advice for older 
adults and those with underlying health conditions who are most at risk, saying they 
should avoid cruises, flights and large gatherings of people.
At a recent Congressional subcommittee hearing, one representative asked Dr. Fauci if he 
had a twin, because he seemed to be everywhere lately. Another offered medical advice: 
lemon, honey and bourbon for his voice, which has been hoarse for weeks from endless 
rounds of talking to lawmakers, scientists, health officials and reporters.
If Dr. Fauci has become the explainer-in-chief of the coronavirus epidemic, it is in part 
because other government scientists have left a vacuum, avoiding the news media 
spotlight or being reined in by the Trump administration and accused of exaggerating the 
threat from the virus. When reporters call Dr. Fauci, he calls them back.
Dr. Robert Redfield, director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, is 
famous for being unknown: He has given few interviews or public talks outside those 
required by administration news conferences. Dr. Nancy Messonnier, director of the 
C.D.C.’s National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases, who warned on
Feb. 25 that the coronavirus was likely to spread in the United States, and that “this could
be bad,” came under fire from the administration and has toned down her advisories.
“Nancy Messonnier told it like it is,” said Dr. Thomas Frieden, the former director of the 
C.D.C. “And she was 100 percent right, and they silenced the messenger.”
The C.D.C. has made few of its other scientists available for interviews about the 
coronavirus. And it is now facing sharp criticism for long delays in providing states with 
kits to test for the virus, and for setting such tight limits on the tests performed at its 
headquarters in Atlanta that some diagnoses were delayed or missed, possibly leaving 
infected people to spread the virus to others.
Dr. Fauci, 79, does not seem to be in the cross hairs. Although he was recently told he 
must clear his many TV, radio and print interviews through the White House, he has said 
that he has not been muzzled.
“You don’t want to go to war with a president,” Dr. Fauci told Politico. But he thinks the 
public needs solid, understandable medical information, especially during crises. He 
makes a point of not trying to “razzle-dazzle” audiences with his knowledge, he told an 
interviewer in 2015, adding that his education at a Jesuit high school and college taught 
him intellectual rigor and the value of public service. As director of the National Institute 
of Allergy and Infectious Diseases since 1984, Dr. Fauci has lasted through six 
presidents, and has declined multiple requests to lead his agency’s parent organization, 
the National Institutes of Health. He has led federal efforts to combat diseases caused by 
emerging viruses, including H.I.V., SARS, the 2009 swine pandemic, MERS, Ebola and 
now the new coronavirus.
He was an architect of the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief, started in 2003 
by President George W. Bush, to fight H.I.V. globally.
In 2001, after anthrax was mailed to Senator Tom Daschle of South Dakota, the Bush 
administration tried initially to minimize the threat, but Dr. Fauci was characteristically 
blunt.
“This is material that is quite formidable, that is infecting people with inhalation anthrax, 
infecting them in the absence of direct contact,” he said. “You can call it whatever you 
want to call it with regard to grade and size or weaponized or not weaponized. The fact 
is, it is acting like a highly efficient bioterrorist agent.”
Previous disease outbreaks have kept him on the lookout for new pathogens, and in 
January, reports of unexplained pneumonia cases in Wuhan, China, set off alarms in his 
head.
“Even before we knew it was a coronavirus, I said it certainly sounds like a coronavirus-
SARS type thing,” he said. “As soon as it was identified, I called a meeting of top-level 
people and said, ‘Let’s start working on a vaccine right now.’”
He is among the most highly paid federal employees, earning about $400,000 a year, 
more than the vice president or the chief justice of the Supreme Court. He oversees a 
2020 budget of $4.75 billion, which is $769 million less than last year’s after being cut by 
the Trump administration.
Unflappable though Dr. Fauci may seem, the new coronavirus worries him, especially its 
spread in the Seattle area and the toll it is taking in a nursing home there. He said he 
thought it was still possible to stop the disease, but health authorities would have to know 
where it was to do that, and he said the lack of testing capacity was a huge obstacle.
Test kits sent by the C.D.C. to states were flawed, and it has taken weeks to begin 
replacing them. And strict regulations from the Food and Drug Administration hampered 
outside labs’ efforts to begin to do their own tests.
But Dr. Fauci declined to join the chorus of blame against the C.D.C.
“It’s so easy to play Monday morning quarterback,” he said. “Every element of the 
federal government was working full-speed to try to get this out and get things going.”
“What I really want to concentrate on is the idea of getting enough tests out there to get 
an evidence-based foundation of where we are in this country,” he said. “Seattle is of 
concern. We need to know the extent of the community spread.”
At times in the past, Dr. Frieden said, Dr. Fauci may have over-promised a bit in his 
enthusiasm for projects of his that have yet to pan out — an H.I.V. vaccine, and a 
universal flu vaccine that would provide long-lasting immunity to multiple strains so that 
people would not need another shot every year.
“It’s the role you have to play to get money from the Hill, and the role of a researcher to 
be eternally optimistic about a cure being around the corner,” Dr. Frieden said. “He’s 
very effective at asking for money from Congress.”
He is also a fair-minded colleague, Dr. Frieden added. During West Africa’s Ebola 
epidemic in 2014, after two nurses treating a patient who had traveled to the United 
States became infected, the C.D.C. was harshly criticized for not having helped hospitals 
to prepare better. Dr. Fauci did not pile on.
“Not everything we did was perfect,” said Dr. Frieden, who then headed the C.D.C. 
“There are many people in similar roles as Tony who might have taken advantage of that 
for the interest of their institution, and Tony was always honorable.”
“If we did something wrong he was frank about that,” he continued. “When we were 
getting attacked unfairly, he defended us. That’s very unusual behavior in the 
bureaucratic situation you see in Washington sometimes. I think that’s why Tony is so 
respected.”
During the early years of the AIDS epidemic, the U.S. government and its health 
agencies were a frequent target of criticism and protests, blamed for inaction on potential 
treatments and inadequate funding for research and medical care.
When AIDS activists demonstrated outside his institute in 1988, demanding a chance to 
try experimental drugs, Dr. Fauci surprised the leaders by inviting them into his office. 
He wound up working with them to develop new ways to expand access without 
compromising the clinical trials that were urgently needed to determine which drugs 
worked — an approach that was later applied to research in other diseases as well.
“There are a lot of world class scientists, but Tony has a special set of skills,” Ms. Shalala 
said. “An ability to communicate, high integrity and an understanding of politics — and 
to know to stay out of politics in order to protect scientists.”
Dr. Fauci acknowledged that his age puts him in one of the groups at highest risk for 
becoming severely ill from a coronavirus infection. But it has not slowed him down. He 
sleeps only about five hours a night, works most of his waking hours and jumps on the 
Metro to get around the Washington, D.C., area, from his office to the Capitol and the 
White House. Most days, he runs or power walks 3.5 miles.
“I’m not worried about myself,” he said. “I’m worried about the job I have to do.”

Anthony Fauci fights outbreaks with the

Dr. Anthony Fauci, the director of the

By 
Karen Tumulty 
Columnist
March 12, 2020 at 5:32 p.m. EDT
A virus that is deadly and little understood. An administration in deep denial. Anthony S. 
Fauci has been here before.
As the coronavirus epidemic escalates, the director of the National Institute of Allergy 
and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) has become a familiar media presence.
Fauci’s expertise and credibility shine against the contradictory and false messages 
coming out of President Trump. The administration has at times sounded more concerned 
with protecting the president politically than stopping the spread of a potentially lethal 
disease.
While Trump tries to play down the severity of a public health crisis that might affect his 
reelection prospects, Fauci has laid out the best assessment of the true danger in stark 
terms.
In testimony Wednesday on Capitol Hill, he warned that the coronavirus has a mortality 
rate 10 times as great as that of the flu, and refuted Trump’s rosy promise that a vaccine 
will be ready “in a fairly quick manner.” Fauci also said flatly that the government is 
“failing” when it comes to the urgent imperative of making widespread testing available.
The latest updates on the coronavirus
After federal officials gave lawmakers a briefing on Thursday, a frustrated Rep. Anna G. 
Eshoo (D-Calif.) told me: “Everything was wrapped in confusion. The only one who 
answers the questions — he not only gives the science, but then he says, let me explain 
this in pedestrian language — is Dr. Fauci.”
Then again, this is not the first time Fauci has found himself in the position of having to 
navigate a public health crisis fraught with political land mines. A renowned international 
expert on the immune system, Fauci took over NIAID in 1984, barely a year and a half 
after scientists had identified a mysterious retrovirus that was killing thousands of people.
It would be nearly another year before President Ronald Reagan would publicly utter the 
name of the disease it produced: AIDS. Reagan’s sluggish handling of the epidemic left 
one of the deepest scars on his legacy.
In 1986, Reagan’s surgeon general, C. Everett Koop, produced a report that described in 
graphic terms the potential toll of AIDS, projecting that 270,000 Americans might 
contract it by 1991. The report used explicit language, explaining that the disease was 
transmitted through “semen and vaginal fluids” and during “oral, anal and vaginal 
intercourse.”
Conservatives approved of some of what was in Koop’s document: It warned against 
“freewheeling casual sex,” and asserted that the surest means of preventing AIDS were 
through abstinence and monogamy. But they weren’t so happy with the surgeon general’s 
recommendation that condoms be used as a fallback.
Koop was concerned that his findings were being buried by the Reagan administration, so 
two years later, he and Fauci cooked up a bold idea: mailing an abridged version of his 
report to every single one of the 107 million households and postal boxes in the country.
The problem, however, was that the surgeon general lacked the budget to do it. As Fauci 
recounted to me during a 2018 interview, he told Koop: “You know, there is a 
mechanism called an interagency transfer.” Fauci had the authority to provide funds to 
get the project off the ground, because combating AIDS related to his own agency’s core 
mission.
Congress picked up the idea and ordered the largest mass mailing in U.S. history. It also 
stipulated that the seven-page brochure be “distributed without necessary clearance of the 
content by any official, organization or office” — in other words, that it not be edited to 
suit anyone’s political agenda.
In addition to being printed in English and Spanish, “Understanding AIDS” went out in 
Chinese, Portuguese, Haitian-Creole, Vietnamese, Laotian, Cambodian and Braille. It 
debunked many myths about the disease, for instance stating unequivocally that AIDS is 
not spread by mosquitoes, and could not be caught through casual contact with saliva, 
sweat or toilet seats.
Subsequent surveys found that nearly 87 million adults perused part or all of the booklet 
— making it the most widely read publication in the country in July 1988, with Reader’s 
Digest coming in a distant second with 48.5 million readers. 
Of course, there are many differences in scale and severity between the AIDS epidemic 
and the coronavirus threat. While most who contract coronavirus will recover, AIDS 
during the 1980s was a death sentence wrapped in stigma.
But as Fauci well understands, all infectious diseases have something in common: 
Accurate information is one of the most powerful weapons for fighting them.
Fauci has already shown how important it is to hit a microscopic enemy with a 
sledgehammer of truth. A yet-untold number of Americans will be betting their lives on 
him to do it again.

election—Anthony Fauci is playing a role in which no previous 
Trump-era figure has survived.
One other person has been in the spot Fauci now occupies. That is, of 
course, James Mattis, the retired four-star Marine Corps general and 
former secretary of defense for Trump. Former is the key word here, 
and the question is whether the change in circumstances between 
Mattis’s time and Fauci’s—the public nature of this emergency, the 
greater proximity of upcoming elections, the apparent verdict from 
financial markets and both international and domestic leaders that 
Donald Trump is in deep over his head—will give Fauci the greater 
leverage he needs, not just to stay at work but also to steer policy 
away from the abyss.
Why is Anthony Fauci now, even more than James Mattis before him, 
in a different position from any other publicly visible associate of 
Trump’s?
1. Pre-Trump credibility, connections, and respect . Fauci has been 
head of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious 
Diseases, at the National Institutes of Health, since Ronald 
Reagan’s first term, in 1984. (How can he have held the post so 
long? Although nothing in his look or bearing would suggest it, 
Fauci is older than either Bernie Sanders or Joe Biden. He 
recently turned 79.)
Through his long tenure at NIH, which spanned the early days 
of the HIV/AIDS devastation and later experience with the 
SARS and H1N1 epidemics, Fauci has become a very familiar 
“public face of science,” explaining at congressional hearings 
and in TV and radio interviews how Americans should think 
about the latest threat. He has managed to stay apart from any 
era’s partisan-political death struggles. He has received a raft of 
scientific and civic honors, from the Lasker Award for health 
leadership, to the Presidential Medal of Freedom, awarded by 
George W. Bush.
Thus, in contrast to virtually all the other figures with whom 
Trump has surrounded himself, Fauci is by any objective 
standard the best person for the job — and is universally seen 
as such . This distinguishes him from people Trump has favored 
in his own coterie, from longtime consigliere Michael Cohen to 
longtime ally Roger Stone to longtime personal 
physician Harold Bornstein; and from past and present 
members of his White House staff, like the departed Michael 
Flynn and the returned Hope Hicks and the sempiternal Jared 
Kushner; and fish-out-of-water Cabinet appointees, like (to 
pick one) the neurosurgeon Ben Carson as Secretary of Housing 
and Urban Development.
Put another way: Very plainly, Trump needs Fauci more than 
Fauci needs Trump. This is not a position Donald Trump has

2. The ability not to abase himself before Trump . The first Cabinet 
meeting Donald Trump held, nearly three years ago, was unlike 
any other conducted in U.S. history, and very much like
